notes: Both address physiological relevance (C6, C53, C59, C68, C71). LLM finds claims UNSUPPORTED due to the substantial gap between experimental (0.1-1 µM ATP) and physiological (mM ATP) conditions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional validation but not outright rejecting the biological relevance. The disagreement reflects different thresholds for evidence sufficiency.

Both evaluate computational modeling claims (C44-C49, C60-C61, C85, C92). LLM finds model UNCERTAIN due to unvalidated assumptions about trailing end behavior. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether simulations provide testable hypotheses. Both agree the modeling contribution requires clarification or additional validation.

Both address ATP-dependent pattern formation (C12, C13, C72). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED based on robust demonstration (94% of n=45 experiments). Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging the use of ~3 µM ATP as non-physiological 'near rigor conditions' versus physiological mM concentrations. Major disagreement on whether low ATP conditions validate the mechanism.

Both evaluate tension-based mechanism (C4, C37, C38). LLM rates UNCERTAIN due to unvalidated assumptions about trailing end behavior. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, directly challenging that the force estimate reflects >80% rigor heads and characterizing the mechanism as an artifact of non-physiological conditions rather than valid biology.

Both address myosin processivity at low ATP (C56, C57). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED based on well-documented experimental evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging the choice of muscle myosin II as 'specialized' and requiring experiments with non-muscle myosin II at physiological ATP concentrations.

Both evaluate force generation model (C62-C65). LLM rates UNCERTAIN, noting the model generates sufficient force but lacks direct validation of key assumptions. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging the experimental design where myosin is free in solution and requiring tethering to invoke physiologically relevant tension.

Partial overlap on ATP-dependent effects (C11, C12). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED with robust sample size. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging fragmentation as 'interesting' but expressing concern about lack of quantification. Disagreement on whether current evidence is sufficient.

Minimal overlap on fragmentation/compaction (C16). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED based on consistent observations (n=21) with quantitative fluorescence data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on experimental replication frequency. Disagreement on adequacy of quantification.

Minimal overlap on single-molecule fragmentation (C21). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED with quantitative tracking of velocity fluctuations and processivity differences. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantification concerns. Disagreement on evidence sufficiency.

Minimal overlap on single-molecule behavior (C22). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED based on correlation between velocity fluctuations and fluorescence. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging the ATP concentration as non-physiological. Disagreement on experimental condition validity.

Minimal overlap on single-molecule experiments (C23). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED with quantitative demonstration. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, characterizing the mechanism as artifact of rigor conditions. Fundamental disagreement on mechanism validity.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic requirements (C52). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED based on connection between low ATP and processivity. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging the ATP concentration as non-physiological. Disagreement on experimental condition validity.

Minimal overlap on MAC system characterization (C10, C99). LLM finds claims SUPPORTED with strong methodological foundation. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging the choice of muscle myosin II as specialized. Disagreement on appropriateness of experimental system.

LLM evaluates MAC system methodology (C8-C10, C97-C104) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review result addresses this specific claim set. Peer reviewers do challenge myosin choice (R5) but don't directly evaluate the MAC system characterization quality.

Limited overlap on mechanism claims (C3). LLM rates tension-based mechanism UNCERTAIN due to unvalidated assumptions. Peer R1 rates fragmentation/compaction UNCERTAIN due to quantification concerns. Both express uncertainty but focus on different aspects of the mechanism.
